summary: Documentation, schemas and tests only: docs/protocol.md (+ German twin) and docs/protocol/*.json specify the existing router-agent tunnel protocol as version 1 (ADR-0107, proposed); test/protocol_schema.py (dependency-free validator), test/selftest_protocol.py (added to ci.yml) and agent/protocol_conformance_test.go bind the specification to the router, the Go agent and test/fake_agent.py. No router or agent code, configuration, version, dependency or wire change. Traced B3: login (challenge, Ed25519 signature over nonce|node|pubkey, 32-KiB hello, enrollment limits, revocation), frame dispatch, request streams and the agent passthrough allowlist were read in registry.py, tunnel.py, poll.py, agent/tunnel.go, passthrough.go, heartbeat.go, facts.go; the documentation matches the code and the new tests now cross-check the allowlist (TM-14), the hello and its refusal cases (TM-07) and the update order fields (TM-13) in CI. B8: update and Ollama update orders are only described, their verification is unchanged. B9: one added CI step with no new action, permission or dependency; AGENTS.md gains a documentation rule and weakens no review policy. Tests bind only loopback (aiohttp TestServer, httptest) and start the fake agent as a subprocess without credentials. The published details (limits, message fields) were already public in the open code; the docs add that the configuration bundle (MQTT password) and the update token are secrets agents must not log. Examples use reserved domains/ranges only. Re-reviewed after merging main (#176, #178, #180, #181, #183) at merge-base 5935bea72e2a: the diff against main is again only this PR's documentation, schemas, tests, CI step and AGENTS.md rule; conflicts were resolved in docs/reference*.md and the ADR index. The schemas were brought up to agent 0.36.0 as the conformance tests demanded (facts and heartbeat gpu_present, GPU values and sensors absent without a GPU, game.enabled, game.via path with the legacy pfad, guard state not_applicable); the router's handling of these fields (registry.node_spec_from_entry, poll.apply_heartbeat, poll.note_game_memory) was read and is described as implemented. The end-to-end self-test now also runs the fake agent without a GPU. No router or agent code changed in this PR.

tests.evidence: Ran 21 tests OK after the merge (Windows, Python 3.12), including both end-to-end runs (fake agent with and without a GPU) through the validating relay and the rejected cases (hello without pubkey/sig/t, 65-character node name, facts not an object -> 401; OLLAMA without up or with non-list tags dropped; POWER with unknown state dropped). Before the schema update it failed naming gpu_present and game.enabled.

ok on Windows after the merge; TestProtocol* failed before the schema update naming Facts.gpu_present, GameFact.enabled and heartbeat gpu_present, and pass now (the heartbeat type table gained gpu_present from GPU.Present).

tests.evidence: 80 steps ok on Windows; the PR-only check_public_changes step was run separately with the merge-base.
No Go toolchain in the local WSL; GOOS=linux go vet passed, CI runs go test on Linux and Windows.
No router Python changed in this PR; the suite is required only for router changes.

limitations: PostgreSQL integrations not run: this PR touches no session, memory or storage code.
Pre-existing, not changed here: a heartbeat the router cannot apply is answered with the exception text in HBACK error to the approved agent; the router fails an open stream on an unknown frame type.

The specification describes what the code does today; it does not prove the absence of protocol flaws. Values and patterns are checked by the Python validator; the Go side checks structure, types and required fields.
